note: The curated reading of the nine toxin entries of the Select Agents and Toxins List as codified at 2024-06-01, for the toxin stratum of the hazard family set (D-204). Hand-curated per entry, as D-137 requires for this list: the pinned data checks the choice and never makes it. Naive protein-name matching is not used, and the Staphylococcal entry below is why.
method: For each toxin entry that names a protein, the reviewed UniProtKB entries that ARE that toxin are chosen by hand, and the Pfam families nominated are the union of those entries' Pfam cross-references. A family is nominated by the entry, not by resembling its name.

entries.note: The four reviewed abrin isoforms (a, b, c, d) of Abrus precatorius. Each is a two-chain protein: an rRNA N-glycosidase A chain and a lectin B chain, so each cross-references both families.
The single reviewed ricin entry of Ricinus communis. Same two-chain architecture as abrin, and the same two families.

The regulation names the toxins in the plural and enumerates no subtypes, so every reviewed botulinum neurotoxin is taken: types A through G, and type X. Including X is a choice and is recorded as one - it was described after the subtype enumerations the list's older readings used, and the entry's own wording does not exclude it. Q45914 cross-references two families the other thirteen do not (PF08470, PF22133), which is why the union is six and not four.

The regulation's own parenthetical limits this entry to subtypes A-E, so SEA, SEB, SEC1, SEC2, SEC3, SED and SEE are taken and the other staphylococcal enterotoxins are not. This is the entry that makes the case against name matching concretely: a case-insensitive match on 'enterotoxin' in this organism also returns SEG, SEH, SEI and enterotoxin-like toxin X, none of which the list names. The families happen to be the same two either way, so nothing in the family set turns on it here - but the method would have been wrong, and on another list it would show.

entries.entry: Conotoxins (Short, paralytic alpha conotoxins containing the following amino acid sequence X1CCX2PACGX3X4X5X6CX7)
entries.note: Declined here rather than guessed. The regulation defines this entry by an amino-acid motif, not by a name, so a name match is the wrong instrument and a family-level nomination would discard the restriction the motif carries - most alpha-conotoxins are not within scope of this entry. Nominating by motif is a separate measurement against a pinned sequence set, and it is not done here.

A trichothecene mycotoxin - a small molecule with no protein sequence, so it nominates no protein family. Same reasoning the hazard set already applies to a listed organism: a regulation naming a molecule nominates no family, and choosing one would be this project's judgement wearing a regulation's authority.
An alkaloid. No protein sequence, so no family. See Diacetoxyscirpenol.
A trichothecene mycotoxin. No protein sequence, so no family. See Diacetoxyscirpenol.
A guanidinium alkaloid. No protein sequence, so no family. See Diacetoxyscirpenol.

flagged.name: Ricin_B_lectin
flagged.why: Nominated by both Abrin and Ricin as the accessory lectin chain, not as the toxic activity - which is PF00161, the rRNA N-glycosidase. Ricin_B_lectin is a carbohydrate-binding domain shared with plant lectins, glycoside hydrolases and much else: 128 reviewed entries carry it against 69 for PF00161, and its prevalence in unreviewed space is far larger. It is kept, because the curated entries do cross-reference it and dropping it would be judgement about which half of a toxin counts. But a detection on PF00652 alone is not evidence of a toxin, and anything reported from this family travels with that sentence.
